description: Discriminator: with row 1 blocked at instance 0 by a record that has no commands and is not committed, does the executor enqueue that instance for recovery? Prefix: the harness prepares the blocked record with the package's own constructor, records the row watermarks in a prerequisite event, and starts the real executeCommands goroutine. Controls: the prerequisite prints the record's status, whether it has commands, crtInstance and ExecedUpTo, and the result prints whether the channel received the instance plus the wall-clock wait as a diagnostic.

harness.description: In-package Go test that blocks one row and waits for the executor's recovery enqueue, reading only the recovery channel.
semantic_changes: harness-only scaffolding: the Replica is constructed in-package and executeCommands is started directly instead of by New(); the loop itself is unmodified
the harness reads instancesToRecover rather than letting the run loop consume it

legality.derivation: The blocked record is the state a replica reaches when it has an instance number but no committed commands for it, and the loop is the implementation's own executor.
legality.applicability: One replica, one blocked row, executor running.
unresolved: the wall-clock length of the grace period is an observation because the counter advances per loop iteration

grounding.derivation: The event reports whether the instance arrived on the recovery channel and which instance it was, which is the duty's observable.
grounding.applicability: The row was blocked and the executor was running.

observable_properties.description: A blocked instance must be enqueued for recovery once the executor's grace period elapses.

uncertainties: the check observes the enqueue, not the recovery it triggers
the grace period's wall-clock length depends on loop iterations, so the measured wait is a diagnostic rather than a specification
